verdict.rationale: A live probe of ReadMe's own ReadMe-hosted docs shows the llms.txt telling agents to 'Append .md to any documentation page URL', which is the story's exact mechanism. The AI-discoverability feature, which scores published pages against an Agent-Friendly Docs spec, reinforces this. Missing for 10: first-party feature docs confirming .md endpoints are served on every customer hub (not just docs.readme.com), the untruncated description of what the .md output contains (clean markdown vs. rendered MDX), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, every published page serves clean markdown at its URL (e.g. appending .md) so agents skip the HTML

citations.quote: Append .md to any documentation page URL to
ReadMe crawls a sample of your published pages and scores your project against the Agent-Friendly Docs spec
